conceptZh: 小玩具機器人想戴上一頂帽子，帽子卻一直滑過頭頂掉到肩膀上、卡在手臂上、掛在腳邊；試了三次之後，他乾脆把頭抬高一點，帽子終於穩穩落在頭上，他立刻擺出超得意的姿勢。
object: a small toy robot and a hat that never lands right
morph: the glyph 頭 stands still as a solid sculpture while the hat gag plays out beside it
creativeAngle: 用「帽子就是戴不到頭上」把注意力反覆導回頭部，三次失敗一次成功的節奏很適合六歲孩子。頭為豆加頁共十六畫，左右都密，字體必須全程靜止。語音詞「頭髮」，頭ㄊㄡˊ、髮ㄈㄚˇ都是單一讀音，也避開和石、木重複的石頭與木頭。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy animation as one continuous locked-off shot on a clean solid pale ivory background. One correctly formed Traditional Chinese character 頭 stands centered the whole time as a flat-fronted sculpture in saturated deep maroon, filling about 70% of the frame height with comfortable margins on all sides. Use standard textbook proportions: the 豆 component on the left and the 頁 component on the right stay clearly separated, with the two dots under 頁 kept apart and every horizontal stroke evenly spaced. The glyph never moves, rotates, tilts or gets covered, and the camera stays locked. Beside its lower right stands a small boxy toy robot, and a soft round hat drops towards him from above. At 0.8 seconds it misses entirely and settles on one shoulder. He shrugs it off and resets, chin up, ready. At 1.6 seconds the hat drops again, bounces off the very top of his head and hooks onto his raised arm instead. He shakes it free, plants his feet more carefully. At 2.4 seconds it drops a third time, slides straight past him and lands neatly over one foot. He stares at it. Beat. At 3.2 seconds he picks it up, stretches his neck upwards as far as it will go to make his head as obvious a target as possible, and drops the hat himself - and this time it lands perfectly. He freezes into an enormously pleased pose, one hand on the brim, then struts out of frame to the right by 4.6 seconds. From 4.7 seconds to 8.0 seconds the frame is completely still and clean, holding on the single centered 頭 with nothing else in shot. Style: Pixar-like glossy chunky toy materials, soft studio lighting, bright high-contrast colors that are vivid but never neon, no dark or moody grading, no white blowouts. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin and says exactly 「頭、頭、頭髮」, using the reading ㄊㄡˊ for 頭 both on its own and inside the word. Speak the first 頭 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 頭髮 around 5.6 seconds while the finished glyph is held still, with natural pauses, then stop; do not keep chanting the character or repeat the line. Keep every sound effect soft and clear of the voice, and use no music louder than the voice. The spoken word is audio only and must not be added to the picture. The only writing anywhere in the frame is the single character 頭: no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no other letters, numbers, watermarks, scenery, extra props, particles, lens flare, motion blur on the glyph, or flashing effects.

conceptZh: 頭：左邊豆，右邊頁，頁代表人的頭；賽車撞到軟墊彈來彈去，每撞一下落一筆，最後點頭。
object: a squeaky pull-back toy race car with googly eyes, a squishy pink cushion wall, and a small knitted safety helmet
morph: the googly-eyed car ricochets between cushions, each bump dropping one stroke of 頭 into place, then it nods to finish
creativeAngle: 賽車衝出去老是衝過頭，在軟墊之間彈來彈去，每撞一下落一筆，最後車頭點點頭，像在說頭字完成了。
promptEn: An 8-second bright, clean toy-animation clip on a solid pale buttercream backdrop. Cast: a squeaky pull-back toy race car, glossy cherry-red with two big googly eyes on its windshield, that always overshoots its target, and a few round pink cushions placed around the frame like bumpers. The only text on screen is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 頭, drawn in saturated royal-blue strokes, ending centered, uncropped, about 70 percent of frame height with margins. 0.0-1.5s: an invisible hand pulls the car backward, the wheels whirring and the googly eyes bulging, and the car zooms forward, misses the first cushion entirely, and slams the left edge with a squeak. The first narrated 頭 lands as it bounces back and the first blue stroke falls from its roof. 1.5-3.5s: the car pinballs from cushion to cushion, boing, squeak, boing, spinning on its wheels, eyes rolling in different directions; each bump drops one more stroke into place, the left part of the glyph first, then the right, while the car's headlamps blink in surprise. The second narrated 頭 lands as the car, dizzy, spins to a stop and the last stroke clicks in, completing 頭. 3.5-5.0s: the car backs up, rolls forward, hits a big pillow and the front of it dips down and up like a polite nod, headlights bobbing. As the word 點頭 is spoken the car nods its hood up and down three times, its googly eyes bouncing, and a little knitted helmet drops from the sky and lands on its roof. 5.0-8.0s: the glyph is perfectly still and fully readable for the last 3 seconds while the car, off to one side, gently rocks on its wheels with the knitted helmet askew, squeaks in a gentle rhythm and blinks its eyes happily, away from the strokes. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks slowly and distinctly in clear Taiwanese Mandarin, clear tones, no erhua, reading exactly these syllables: 頭、頭、點頭 (ㄊㄡˊ、ㄊㄡˊ、ㄉㄧㄢˇ ㄊㄡˊ). The character twice with a short pause, then the word once, then stop. The word is audio only. No background music, no extra speech, no subtitles or flashing effects; stylized toy vehicles only, no real people.

conceptZh: 太空人玩偶的魚缸頭盔一直飄在頭上方扣不下去，調皮小老鼠想幫忙「輕輕拍一下」，卻用力過猛衝過頭，撞翻角落一疊橘色長條，長條散落剛好排成「頭」；老鼠冒煙倒滑回來，最後用一根手指輕輕一點，頭盔喀一聲扣上，太空人開心敲敲頭盔。
object: a cheeky toy mouse, a bouncy astronaut toy whose fishbowl helmet keeps floating off its head, and a tall stack of orange bars
morph: the mouse overshoots the helmet, slams the stack of bars, and the bars rain down into the strokes of 頭, left 豆 first then right 頁, finishing with the two feet dots
creativeAngle: 前兩版是「帽子戴不上」與「賽車彈來彈去」，這次改用「用力過猛」的慢動作鋪陳：目標是極小的一下輕拍（把頭盔扣回頭上），小老鼠卻火力全開衝過頭，撞散的長條直接落成字形，第二次輕輕一點才成功，六歲孩子一看就懂「太用力 vs 剛剛好」。詞選「頭盔」（盔只有ㄎㄨㄟ一讀），因為太空人的魚缸頭盔本身就是畫面主角，說到詞的瞬間頭盔正好喀一聲扣上，聲音與畫面完全對應。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy-animation clip, one continuous locked-off shot on a clean solid pale sky-blue background with soft studio lighting, glossy chunky toy materials, bright high-contrast colors that are vivid but never neon, no dark grading and no white blowouts. The only text that ever appears is the single Traditional Chinese character 頭, built from saturated tangerine-orange bars with rounded ends; when finished it stands centered and uncropped, filling about 70 percent of the frame height with comfortable margins, in standard textbook proportions: the 豆 component on the left (a short top horizontal, a 口 box, two small dots, a long bottom horizontal) and the 頁 component on the right, slightly wider (a top horizontal, a short left-falling stroke, a 目 box, and two separate feet dots at the bottom). Every horizontal is evenly spaced, the two components stay clearly apart, and once complete the glyph never moves, tilts or gets covered.

Cast, kept small along the bottom lane so they never overlap the glyph zone: the lead is an original tiny cheeky cartoon mouse, lavender-grey with huge round pink ears, a whip-thin tail and a permanent mischievous grin, lightning fast. The buddy is a bouncy original astronaut toy in a white padded suit with yellow trim and a clear fishbowl helmet; the helmet keeps floating a hand-width above his head and he keeps bobbing up to meet it and missing. At the far right edge stands a tall neat stack of the tangerine bars.

0.0 to 1.2 seconds: the astronaut toy stands in the lower right, hopping up at his floating helmet, bonk, miss, bonk, miss. The mouse at the lower left spots the problem, points one finger at the helmet, rolls up imaginary sleeves and nods: tiny job, one little tap. 1.2 to 2.5 seconds: instead of walking over, the mouse digs in its heels, pins its ears back, and its legs spin into a whirring blur like an outboard motor, dust puffing, the frame trembling slightly with far too much wind-up for the task. The first spoken 頭 lands as it launches at about 1.4 seconds. It rockets right as a pink streak, blows straight past the astronaut so fast the floating helmet spins like a top, and slams into the stack of bars at about 2.3 seconds with a big soft BONK: squash, stretch, bars fountaining up into the air. 2.5 to 3.9 seconds: the mouse skids backwards across the floor on its feet with little smoke curls rising from its toes, eyes spinning in spirals, grin still on. Overhead the bars tumble down and click into place one after another in the center: the 豆 component lands on the left first, then the 頁 component on the right, and the two feet dots drop in last. The second spoken 頭 lands as that last dot clicks at about 3.6 seconds, and the finished 頭 is fully readable from 3.9 seconds onward. 3.9 to 5.4 seconds: the mouse shakes its head clear, trots calmly back to the astronaut, raises a single fingertip, takes a dainty breath, and taps the drifting helmet once, tink. The helmet sinks neatly onto the astronaut's head and seals with a soft pop. The word 頭盔 is spoken exactly on that tap at about 5.0 seconds while the astronaut proudly raps his knuckles on the dome. 5.4 to 8.0 seconds: the glyph stays perfectly still and clear for the whole hold. In the lower right the astronaut drifts gently off the ground anyway, helmet now firmly on, and bumps softly against nothing, while the mouse polishes his helmet with its tail and gives a silent giggle and a thumbs-up. Neither character touches or crosses the strokes.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks slowly and distinctly in clear Taiwanese Mandarin, Taiwan standard readings, clear tones, no erhua, reading exactly these syllables: 頭、頭、頭盔 (ㄊㄡˊ、ㄊㄡˊ、ㄊㄡˊ ㄎㄨㄟ). The character twice with a short pause between, then the word once, then stop; do not keep chanting the character or repeat the line. The spoken word is audio only and never appears as text. Sound effects are soft cartoon whirs, bonks and tinks kept quieter than the voice, with no music louder than the voice. No subtitles, no other letters or numbers, no watermark, no scenery clutter, no flashing effects, no motion blur on the glyph. Stylized toy characters only, no real people, no realistic humans, no presenter on screen.
